## Validations Tab

The Validations tab under the Product Editor contains datetime effective fields where the user can set up validation limits for Density, Correction Factors (CTL, CPL and CTPL), Product Specifications, Net Allowable, and Mass Allowable.

There are no default limits set for Product Specification, Net Allowable, or Mass Allowable fields.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Density">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Density</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Density">

Here, users can specify the number of decimal places (discrimination level) that imported values for Density Factors will rounded to in order to verify that they are the same as the FLOWCAL calculated values. An exception is generated if the rounded import value does not match the FLOWCAL calculated value. The **Run on Imports and Edits** checkbox must be checked for the validation to occur.

Density and Correction Factors contain default limits (set initially when FLOWCAL is installed) that may be modified. The limits dictate the number of decimal places displayed in FLOWCAL and on printed reports for each field.

**Example:** Meter flowing density is imported in a CFX file and is also calculated by FLOWCAL from the observed density. If the imported value is in API Degrees and the Rounding Factor for API Degrees is set to one, then the imported value will be rounded to one decimal place before being compared to the FLOWCAL calculated value.

The Primary Density Calc Method is available for products with a calculation table of Table-E (TP-27), Table-E Extended (TP-27 EXT), COSTALD, or Modified TP-2. The options are COSTALD and Modified TP-2. The selected Primary Density Calc Method will be used on meter batches to calculate a density based on the provided analysis at the observed density conditions. This density can be used to validate the observed density.

When a sample is manually entered in an LQ source or as a standalone sample, then the sample follows the setup of Sample Density Calc. Method as the default calculation for the Base Density Calc Method. The user can manually override this default when entering or editing a sample.

For Products using Table-E (TP-27) or Table-E Extended (TP-27 EXT), the user may choose to Use Relative Density from Analysis As Observed, if Observed Density is Missing and to Use Relative Density from Analysis In TP-15 Calc. instead of Observed Density. Standalone tickets using a Table E product follow the setup on the product for these two options. Meters follow the setup for these two options on the product, unless these options have a different setup at the meter level.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Correction">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Correction Factors</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Correction">

Here the number of decimal places (discrimination level) may be specified for where rounding is done on CTL, CPL and CTPL for calculation of the Combined Correction Factor (CCF).

CCF = Round(meter factor,x) \* Round(CTL,y) \* Round(CPL,z)

**where:** x, y and z are discrimination levels defined in the Product Editor for each field

If the **Use Rounded CTPL in CCF** application option is selected, then the precision specified here for CTPL will be used.

In this case:

CCF = Round(meter factor,x) \* Round(Round(CTL,y) \* Round(CPL,z),w)

**where:** w, x, y and z are discrimination levels defined in the Product Editor for each field with w being the precision defined for CTPL



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Product Spec">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Product Spec</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Product Spec">

On the Product Spec. and Product Spec.2 sub-tabs, users can specify the minimum and maximum limits for components and other data points that are applied to liquid quality sources, liquid meters, and tickets.

The Percent Type field specifies whether the limits are by: Mole %, Liquid Volume %, Mass %, or PPM.

Limits for Product Spec.2 properties that do not have the percent type are by unit.

[Exceptions 30009 - 30040](../../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/30000/30000-30999.md) and [exceptions 4800 - 4860](../../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/4000/4800-4899.md) are generated for records outside of the specified limits for the product.

The **Run on Imports and Edits** option must be selected for the validation to occur.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" /> 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Net Alloable">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Net Allowable</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Net Alloable">

On the Net Allowable tab, users can specify net allowable limits per product. FLOWCAL calculates component volumes and component mass for meters and tickets based on the analysis applied. Once these have been calculated, net allowable limits are applied. Component volumes above the net allowable limits are removed from the net allowable component volumes. Net allowable component volumes can be viewed in the Volume Editor and the Ticket Editor, as well as on numerous Net Allowable reports. Limits that can be specified for Net Allowable amount are:

- The volume of CO2 allowed as a percentage of ethane volume
- The volume of nitrogen allowed as a percentage of total component volume
- The volume of methane allowed can be specified as the minimum or the maximum of the following:
  - Percentage of total component volume less nitrogen and CO2
  - Percentage of ethane
  - Percentage of ethane and heavier (C2 - C10).

When specified, if the value of methane, nitrogen or CO2 exceeds the specified limits, the allowed amount is calculated and appears on batch reports and in various editors and rollup viewers. These are set based on product specifications for each customer’s company. Typically, there is no value in CO2 or nitrogen and the net allowable amounts for these two components is zero.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Mass Allowable">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Mass Allowable</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Mass Allowable">

Mass Allowable calculations only apply to non-hydrocarbon components. The Mass Allowable tab is enabled when a non-hydrocarbon fluid service is selected on the Products tab. On the Mass Allowable tab, non-hydrocarbon components can be rolled into one another and maximum limits can be set for the component mass percent.

If enabled, when component values are calculated for non-hydrocarbon components, FLOWCAL will roll specified components into one another and apply mass allowable limits. Once a component is rolled into another component, it cannot be rolled again and a max mass percent cannot be specified. Components also cannot roll into a component that is already rolled into something else.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 613;height: 452;" />

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Mass Allowable Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

<div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Mass Allowable Example">

If hydrogen is rolled into helium:

- The Max Mass % field for hydrogen will be disabled.
- The component drop-down for helium will be disabled.

If another component is then selected to roll into hydrogen:

- A message will display, stating that there is an invalid selection, and the selection will not be saved.
